title: Invocation modes: fail‑fast vs best‑effort streaming contract PRD
creator: Marcus Lee
description: Problem statement: Customers building multi-step LLM flows need predictable semantics when the model requests external tool/function invocations during streaming responses. Current ambiguity around partial emissions, backpressure, and retry semantics forces teams to build brittle ad-hoc workarounds. This PRD defines two supported invocation modes (fail‑fast and best‑effort), the streaming checkpoint contract, observable contract events, and a developer test harness for contract validation.
scope: Define API-level flags and behavioral guarantees for two invocation modes. Specify streaming checkpoint envelope format, idempotency token behavior, retry/backoff guidance, telemetry events, and SDK compatibility expectations across hosted and Dedicated deployments. Provide acceptance tests and a lightweight reference harness for end-to-end validation.
out_of_scope: Language model training changes, model architecture modifications, deep runtime kernel tuning, and billing model changes. Detailed UI implementation for the Console will be handled in a follow-up ticket.
success_metrics: Reduction in customer-reported broken tool-handoffs by 70% within first 3 months
Automated contract test coverage added to CI for 90% of supported SDK languages
Default mode adoption: >=60% of new integrations use 'best-effort' mode where appropriate
acceptance_criteria: Mode flag: API accepts invocation_mode={"fail_fast"|"best_effort"} with default=fail_fast and the mode is recorded in request logs

Fail‑fast semantics: if a requested tool invocation fails synchronously (validation / quick auth failure) or times out within the configured tool_timeout, the entire response stream terminates with an explicit terminal frame {"type":"error","code":"tool_failure","detail":<human_message>} and HTTP status 424 for non-streaming calls

Best‑effort semantics: failed tool invocations are emitted as recoverable frames {"type":"tool_error","retryable":<true|false>,"id":<invocation_id>,"detail":<short>} and the stream continues to emit subsequent structured objects; the final envelope includes a summary of tool invocation outcomes

Streaming checkpoints: model output must include checkpoint frames at least every 4KB or 10s (whichever is first) with a deterministic checkpoint_id; checkpoint frame schema is documented and validated by contract tests

Idempotency tokens: each tool invocation includes invocation_id and idempotency_token; system honors repeated invocations with same idempotency_token within 24 hours and returns previously recorded outcome or replay marker

Partial object recovery: when a stream resumes after a transient transport interruption, client may request missing checkpoint_id range and the server will provide replayed frames or a reconciliation summary if full replay is not available

Backpressure signal: SDKs expose an optional application-level backpressure header X-Client-Buffering:{"low"|"normal"|"high"} and the service uses it as advisory for batch scheduling; absence of header does not change correctness guarantees

Observability hooks: contract_events emitted to telemetry for every invocation and final outcome using event names: invocation.requested, invocation.started, invocation.completed, invocation.failed, invocation.replayed; each event includes invocation_id, mode, model_version, route, and latency_ms
Error classification: errors are labelled as transient|permanent|policy; acceptance tests assert that transient errors surface with retryable=true and permanent errors have retryable=false

SDK behavior: official SDKs (Python/Node/Go) implement high-level helpers to parse checkpoint frames, surface tool errors as typed exceptions, and offer helper to resume missing checkpoints using replay APIs

Compatibility: Dedicated and Private deployments must implement identical semantic surface for modes and checkpoints; a feature-flag compatibility layer is acceptable during rollout with explicit deprecation timeline

Test harness: provide an automated contract test suite that can run against hosted and Dedicated endpoints; suite includes simulated tool latency/failure scenarios and verifies correct frames, telemetry emission, and idempotency behavior
implementation_notes: Runtime: add lightweight invocation_mode routing in the API layer and include mode in routing/quotas/logs
Gateway: ensure streaming envelope parser tags checkpoint frames and forwards invocation metadata to tool worker pool
Tool workers: must surface structured error objects with canonical codes and honor idempotency tokens
SDKs: add new helpers parse_stream_checkpoints() and resume_from_checkpoint(checkpoint_id, options)
Observability: add new dashboards for invocation success rate, replay rate, and average time-to-complete per invocation mode
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable feature flag for 10% of hosted traffic and Dedicated customers who opt-in. Run contract test harness nightly. Phase 2: default to fail_fast for backward compatibility and publish SDK helpers. Phase 3: make best_effort the recommended pattern for multi-tool orchestrations and provide migration guide.
